title: Remove or wire up SettingsCodec.encode — zero callers in lib/ or test/
why: grep -rn 'SettingsCodec()' across lib/ and test/ finds only the decode-side caller in settings_merger.dart — nothing calls .encode(), unlike bookmark/track/goal/etc. where encode() is the live push path. A symmetric but unreachable encode() looks load-bearing to a reader and invites either a false assumption that it's exercised, or silent drift from the real settings push shape with nothing to notice if it ever changes.
recommendation: Either wire SettingsCodec.encode into whatever currently constructs the settings push payload, or delete it and note in the class doc that settings is currently pull/decode-only.
acceptance_criteria: grep for 'SettingsCodec().encode' or 'SettingsCodec.encode' in lib/ returns at least one production call site, OR the method is removed with a comment explaining decode-only status.

corrections: encode() is an abstract override required by EntityCodec<T> (entity_codec.dart:59) — SettingsCodec cannot simply delete the method without breaking the interface contract; a throwing stub with an explanatory comment is the realistic 'delete' path, not literal removal. Minor recommendation imprecision only, doesn't undermine the core dead-code finding.
